query: What visit reasons point to different departments?

per_column.name: primary_reason
per_column.rationale: This is a normalized/extracted version of the reason_for_visit, capturing the chief complaint (e.g., 'well-child visit', 'sports physical', 'diabetes follow-up'). The visit reason lies outside the department and is precisely the signal the query targets for pointing to departments. It is knowable at intake (pre-outcome), so no leakage. Its main weakness is high cardinality/near-uniqueness, but semantically it carries strong predictive signal about department.

per_column.name: condition_category
per_column.rationale: A rolled-up clinical category of the visit reason (Preventive_Care, Musculoskeletal_Issue, Cardiovascular_Issue, etc.). This is a derived predictor from the reason text, external to department, available at intake, and generalizes the reason into a low-cardinality feature that plausibly maps strongly to departments. Legitimate, high-utility predictor.

judge.rationale: Both added columns are legitimate, non-leaking predictors of department derived from the visit reason, directly matching the analytical intent of finding which reasons point to which departments. condition_category is especially useful: it converts the free-text reason into a compact, generalizable categorical feature that a model can leverage. primary_reason adds signal but its extreme cardinality limits standalone leverage. As a set they add meaningful predictive leverage beyond the raw reason_for_visit text, though they are transformations of an existing column rather than genuinely new external variables, capping the incremental utility.
